title: Stores and Logistics Meeting Decisions (2024-10-01)
summary: Operational decisions agreed on 2024-10-01 covering stores job order bookings, inter-site van transfers, pallet dispatch staging, return quarantine labelling, and packaging stock counts.

infobox.Decision-makers: Isla Morgan, Pieter Jansen, Joanna Fletcher

body:
On 2024-10-01, operational leadership established procedural decisions addressing material control, transfer timing, and warehouse congestion across Northbridge facilities [^r1][^r2][^r3]. The agreed rules require immediate electronic logging of issues and inter-site movements, formal quarantine tagging for bike shop returns, and rigorous cycle counting of packaging lines [^r1][^r3][^r4][^r5]. These decisions remain in force to ensure inventory accuracy and prevent logistics bottlenecks [^r1][^r2][^r3].

## Agreed operational decisions

### Material issues to production
[[user-imorgan|Isla Morgan]], [[user-pjansen|Pieter Jansen]], and [[user-jfletcher|Joanna Fletcher]] agreed that stores hands must log material issues against the correct job orders on the terminal prior to raw castings and bought-in electrical sub-assemblies leaving holding pens for the assembly line [^r1].

### Inter-site transfers between Manchester and Leeds
Staff at Manchester and the Leeds satellite unit must execute goods-out and goods-in transfer routines directly in Ledgerline on the day the van arrives, eliminating reliance on delayed manual inter-site delivery notes [^r3].

### Dispatch staging and carrier collections
Dispatch staff in Manchester must strap and label pallets earlier in the afternoon to prevent dispatch bay congestion caused by primary carrier collection delays past the agreed cut-off [^r2].

### Bike shop returns and quarantine
A clear quarantine label must be affixed to every returned crate from bike shops immediately upon offloading from the carrier, and the sales office must provide the corresponding paperwork promptly [^r4].

### Packaging inventory tracking
Basic dispatch packaging lines, including cardboard cartons and packing foam, must be integrated into the weekly perpetual inventory count rota rather than estimated through informal visual checks [^r5].
